title_en: Sun Lixing v. Tianjin Park Labor Bureau — administrative dispute over work-related injury determination
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 14(1) of the Regulations on Industrial Injury Insurance, an employee who suffers an accident injury during working hours and at the workplace due to work-related reasons shall be determined as having a work-related injury. The terms 'workplace' and 'due to work-related reasons' in this provision should be comprehensively and correctly interpreted. 'Workplace' refers to the place where an employee engages in occupational activities. In the case of multiple workplaces, it also includes the necessary areas through which employees travel between multiple workplaces. 'Due to work-related reasons' means that there is a causal relationship between the employee's injury and the performance of their job duties, i.e., the employee is injured because of performing their own work. Except for the circumstances specified in Article 16 of the Regulations on Industrial Injury Insurance, such as injuries or deaths caused by crimes or violations of public security administration, injuries or deaths caused by intoxication, self-inflicted injuries or suicide, the existence of negligence on the part of the employee while performing work does not affect the establishment of this causal relationship.

full_text_en:
Sun Lixing v. Tianyuan District Labor Bureau

Dispute over Administrative Determination of Work-Related Injury

Ruling Summary

According to Article 14(1) of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance, an employee who suffers an accident injury during working hours and at the workplace due to work-related reasons shall be determined as having a work-related injury. The terms "workplace" and "due to work-related reasons" in this provision shall be comprehensively and correctly interpreted. "Workplace" refers to the place where an employee engages in professional activities, and in the case of multiple workplaces, it also includes the necessary areas through which the employee travels between multiple workplaces; "due to work-related reasons" means that there is a causal relationship between the employee's injury and the performance of his or her own work, i.e., the employee is injured because of engaging in his or her own work. Except for the circumstances specified in Article 16 of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance, such as injuries or deaths caused by crimes or violations of public security administration, injuries or deaths caused by intoxication, self-inflicted injuries or suicide, etc., if an employee is negligent in the course of work, such negligence does not affect the establishment of the causal relationship.

Plaintiff: Sun Lixing, male, 58 years old, employee of Tianjin Zhongli Lightning Protection Technology Co., Ltd., residing at Baoshan Beili, Baoshan Road, Nankai District, Tianjin.

Defendant: Tianjin New Technology Industrial Park Labor and Personnel Bureau, domiciled at Haitai Building, Huayuan Industrial Park, Nankai District, Tianjin.

Legal Representative: Wang Jianying, Director of this Bureau.

Third Party: Tianjin Zhongli Lightning Protection Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at International Business Center, Huayuan Industrial Park, Nankai District, Tianjin.

Legal Representative: Sun Weiwei, General Manager of this Company.

Plaintiff Sun Lixing, dissatisfied with the work-related injury determination decision made by Defendant Tianjin New Technology Industrial Park Labor and Personnel Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the Park Labor Bureau), filed an administrative lawsuit with the Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court. The Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court considered that the plaintiff's employer, Tianjin Zhongli Lightning Protection Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongli Company), had an interest in the alleged specific administrative act, and therefore notified Zhongli Company to participate in the proceedings as a third party.

Plaintiff Sun Lixing alleged: The plaintiff was an employee of the third party Zhongli Company. On June 10, 2003, Sun Lei, the person in charge of Zhongli Company, instructed the plaintiff to drive the company's Red Flag car to Beijing Airport to pick up someone before 11:00 a.m. that day, and incidentally to first deliver a batch of goods near the Zhou Enlai and Deng Yingchao Memorial Hall. After receiving the task, the plaintiff immediately went to the company's competent department to collect the car keys and gasoline coupons, went through the relevant formalities, and then hurried downstairs to get the car. When reaching the steps at the entrance on the first floor, due to the slippery ground and his haste, the plaintiff fell from the fourth step and was injured. After the accident, although Zhongli Company immediately sent someone to take the plaintiff to the hospital for treatment, it stopped paying medical expenses and wages from September 2003 and did not admit that the plaintiff was injured on duty. After the plaintiff applied twice, the defendant Park Labor Bureau issued the (2004) No. 0001 "Work-Related Injury Determination Decision" on March 5, 2004, deciding not to determine the plaintiff's fall accident as a work-related injury on the grounds that there was no evidence showing that the fall accident was caused by work-related reasons. The plaintiff fell and was injured during working hours, at the workplace, and due to work-related reasons, which falls under the circumstances specified in Article 14(1) of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance. The decision made by the defendant based on Article 14(5) of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance had incorrect factual findings and improper application of law. The plaintiff requested the court to annul the defendant's (2004) No. 0001 "Work-Related Injury Determination Decision" and order the defendant to make a new determination.

The plaintiff submitted the following evidence:

1. The (2004) No. 0001 "Work-Related Injury Determination Decision" made by the defendant Park Labor Bureau, which stated: At approximately 10:20 a.m. on June 10, 2004, Sun Lixing, a business clerk of Zhongli Company, slipped at the steps of the entrance on the first floor of the International Business Center (hereinafter referred to as the Business Center) in Huayuan Industrial Park, fell from the fourth step and landed on his front side, causing Sun Lixing to suffer a cervical spinal hyperextension injury combined with cervical nerve root traction injury, upper lip contusion and laceration, abrasion on the left arm, and abrasion on the left leg. Based on the injured employee's own work-related injury application and medical diagnosis certificate, combined with the relevant investigation materials collected by this bureau, and in accordance with the determination standard of Article 14(5) of Chapter III of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance promulgated by State Council Order No. 375, we consider that there is no evidence showing that Sun Lixing's fall accident was caused by work-related reasons, and therefore decide not to determine Sun Lixing's fall accident as a work-related injury accident.

2. Two photos, used to prove the scene of the plaintiff's fall injury.

3. Maintenance documents for the Red Flag car, used to prove that the plaintiff also maintained the Red Flag car of Zhongli Company in April 2003.

4. The plaintiff's work badge at Zhongli Company from May 2003, used to prove that the plaintiff was indeed an employee of Zhongli Company.

Defendant Park Labor Bureau argued: Upon investigation, Sun Lixing, a business clerk of Zhongli Company, was injured during a business trip outside, but the injury was not due to work-related reasons, but due to his own lack of concentration and stepping on air, causing him to fall when going down the steps. There was no obvious causal relationship between his injury and the work task he had received, so it did not fall under the circumstances that should be determined as a work-related injury under Article 14(5) of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance. The defendant's decision not to determine a work-related injury based on Article 14(5) of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance had clear factual findings, sufficient evidence, and lawful procedures, and the court should uphold it.

The defendant provided the following evidence:

1. The Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance, used to prove that the defendant had the subject qualification and authority to make work-related injury determinations, and that the content and procedures of the work-related injury determination decision were lawful.

2. Sun Lixing's application form for work-related injury determination, used to prove that the work-related injury determination decision was made upon Sun Lixing's own application.

3. Copy of ID card, business card, labor contract, and salary passbook, used to prove that a labor relationship existed between Sun Lixing and Zhongli Company.

4. Sun Lixing's medical records and diagnostic certificate, used to prove the fact of Sun Lixing's injury.

5. Interview records with Sun Lei, Wu Shilun, Liu Wei, Liu Chunsheng, Pang Lishuang, Yang Xuezhang, Sun Weiwei, etc., the main content of which was to prove that Sun Lixing was an employee of the Marketing Department, had a labor relationship with the third party, and had collected gasoline coupons from Zhongli Company before the injury to prepare for a business trip, etc.

Third Party Zhongli Company stated: Because the company implemented a last-place elimination system, plaintiff Sun Lixing had been eliminated before the incident. However, because he originally engaged in the company's sales work and still had the obligation to collect remaining payments, he occasionally returned to the company to make phone calls. At the time of the incident, Sun Lixing was no longer an employee of the company and did not fall within the company's workplace area, so he did not meet the conditions for determining a work-related injury.

The third party did not provide evidence.

During the court trial and cross-examination, plaintiff Sun Lixing had no objection to evidence 2-5 submitted by defendant Park Labor Bureau, but argued that he was injured while receiving instructions from his leadership during normal working hours to complete work tasks, which fell under Article 14(1) of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance, and Article 14(5) should not apply, and that evidence 1 submitted by the defendant could not prove that the content of the work-related injury determination was lawful. The Park Labor Bureau had no objection to the evidence submitted by Sun Lixing. The third party Zhongli Company raised no objection to the evidence submitted by either Sun Lixing or the Park Labor Bureau.

After cross-examination, the Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court confirmed the evidence: The evidence submitted by plaintiff Sun Lixing was lawful, true, and relevant to the case, and should be confirmed; evidence 2-5 submitted by defendant Park Labor Bureau were the factual basis for the specific administrative act of the Park Labor Bureau, the form of evidence acquisition was lawful, the content was objective and true, and should be admitted; evidence 1 was a legal provision that should be applied in this case.

The Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court found upon trial:

Plaintiff Sun Lixing was an employee of the third party Zhongli Company. On the morning of June 10, 2003, the person in charge of Zhongli Company assigned Sun Lixing to drive a car to Beijing Airport to pick up someone. Sun Lixing then went downstairs from the eighth floor of the Business Center where Zhongli Company was located, preparing to go to the parking area within the Business Center compound where the company's Red Flag car was parked. When reaching the steps at the entrance on the first floor, Sun Lixing slipped, fell from the fourth step to the ground, and was unable to move his limbs. Zhongli Company immediately sent someone to take Sun Lixing to the First Affiliated Hospital of Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine for treatment. The hospital diagnosed him with cervical spinal hyperextension injury combined with cervical nerve root traction injury, upper lip contusion and laceration, abrasion on the left arm, and abrasion on the left leg. Sun Lixing applied to the defendant Park Labor Bureau for a work-related injury determination. After investigation and verification, the Park Labor Bureau issued the (2004) No. 0001 "Work-Related Injury Determination Decision" on March 5, 2004, deciding not to determine Sun Lixing's fall accident as a work-related injury accident on the grounds that there was no evidence showing that the fall accident was caused by work-related reasons. Sun Lixing was dissatisfied and filed this administrative lawsuit.

The Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court held:

Based on the existing evidence, at the time of the incident, plaintiff Sun Lixing was an employee of the third party Zhongli Company. Zhongli Company claimed that Sun Lixing was no longer an employee of the company at the time of the incident, but did not submit corresponding evidence, so this claim was not accepted. According to the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance and the Measures for Determining Work-Related Injuries promulgated by the Ministry of Labor and Social Security as Order No. 17, the defendant Park Labor Bureau had the subject qualification to be responsible for work-related injury insurance work within its administrative region, and accepting applications for work-related injury determination and making work-related injury determination decisions fell within its scope of functions and powers. The procedure by which the Park Labor Bureau made the work-related injury determination decision on Sun Lixing's fall accident upon his application complied with the relevant provisions of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance and the Measures for Determining Work-Related Injuries.

Article 14(1) of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance stipulates that an employee who suffers an accident injury during working hours and at the workplace due to work-related reasons shall be determined as having a work-related injury. Article 14(5) stipulates that an employee who is injured due to work-related reasons or goes missing due to an accident during a business trip outside shall be determined as having a work-related injury. After receiving the task assigned by the company's leadership to drive and pick up someone, plaintiff Sun Lixing went downstairs from the eighth floor where the company was located to the first floor, and fell on the way to the parking area within the compound where the car was parked. Sun Lixing had not yet driven the car out of the company's compound, so the fall did not occur during a business trip outside, but rather occurred during working hours and at the workplace, and he fell due to work-related reasons in order to complete the work task. Therefore, it met the statutory conditions for determining a work-related injury under Article 14(1) of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance. Accordingly, the (2004) No. 0001 "Work-Related Injury Determination Decision" made by the defendant Park Labor Bureau based on Article 14(5) of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance applied the law incorrectly and should be annulled.

Based on this, the Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 54(2) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Administrative Procedure Law) and Article 59(1) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on March 23, 2005, rendered the following judgment:

1. Annul the (2004) No. 0001 "Work-Related Injury Determination Decision" made by the defendant Park Labor Bureau on March 5, 2004;

2. The defendant Park Labor Bureau shall make a new specific administrative act within 60 days from the date this judgment takes effect.

The Park Labor Bureau was dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment and appealed to the Tianjin High People's Court. The reasons were: The bureau determined that the appellee Sun Lixing was "on a business trip outside," which was clear in fact. The business premises of the original third party Zhongli Company were on the eighth floor of the Business Center, and the task assigned to the appellee was to drive and pick up someone. According to common understanding, only the business premises of Zhongli Company on the eighth floor of the Business Center and the car driven by the appellee were the appellee's workplaces. The appellee fell at the steps of the entrance on the first floor of the Business Center, and the location of the fall was not within the scope of the appellee's workplace. The appellee did not fall due to completing the work task, i.e., while driving, nor due to objective reasons such as slippery steps caused by rain or snow, but entirely due to his own lack of concentration, so it did not constitute an injury "due to work-related reasons." The first-instance judgment found that the appellee's fall accident occurred at the "workplace" and that the appellee fell "to complete the work task," which was erroneous in factual findings and incorrect in application of law. The appellant requested the annulment of the first-instance judgment and a judgment upholding the appellant's (2004) No. 0001 "Work-Related Injury Determination Decision."

Appellee Sun Lixing argued: The appellee's employer, Zhongli Company, was located on the eighth floor of the Business Center, and the company's vehicles were parked within the Business Center compound. Therefore, the steps at the entrance on the first floor of the Business Center were a necessary path for the appellee to complete the work task of driving and picking up someone. The appellee received the task with urgency and slipped while walking quickly to complete the work, which fell under the statutory "accident injury due to work-related reasons." The first-instance judgment correctly found that the appellee was injured during working hours, at the workplace, and due to work-related reasons, and should be upheld.

Original third party Zhongli Company argued: 1. The appellee's work task on that day was to drive and pick up someone, so his workplace should have been inside the car. 2. Whether the working time was urgent was not directly related to the appellee's fall. The interpretation of "due to work-related reasons" should not be overly broad. 3. In the absence of clear legal provisions, the understanding and determination of the law by the appellant, as an administrative organ, should be respected. The appellee was injured during an outing, and it did not fall under the circumstances that should be determined as a work-related injury under the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance. The appellant's (2004) No. 0001 "Work-Related Injury Determination Decision" applied the law correctly.

The Tianjin High People's Court, upon trial, confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

The Tianjin High People's Court held:

All parties had no objection to the first-instance judgment's determination that the appellant Park Labor Bureau had administrative subject qualification and statutory authority, that its work-related injury determination decision complied with statutory procedures, and that the appellee Sun Lixing fell during working hours. Therefore, the disputed issues in this case were: 1. Was the location where Sun Lixing fell within the scope of the "workplace"? 2. Did Sun Lixing fall "due to work-related reasons"? 3. Did Sun Lixing's own negligence in walking affect the work-related injury determination?

Regarding the issue of whether the location where the appellee Sun Lixing fell was within the scope of the "workplace": The "workplace" as stipulated in Article 14(1) of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance refers to the place where an employee engages in professional activities, and in the case of multiple workplaces, it also includes the necessary areas through which the employee travels between multiple workplaces. In this case, the office of Zhongli Company on the eighth floor of the Business Center was Sun Lixing's workplace, and the car he needed to drive to complete the task was another workplace of Sun Lixing. The car was parked outside the entrance on the first floor of the Business Center. To complete the driving task, Sun Lixing had to go from the eighth floor of the Business Center to the parking area outside the first-floor entrance. Therefore, the area from the eighth floor of the Business Center to the parking area was a necessary area through which Sun Lixing traveled between two workplaces and should also be regarded as Sun Lixing's workplace. The appellant Park Labor Bureau's assertion that the fall location was not within Sun Lixing's workplace excluded the necessary path for completing the work task from the workplace, which was inconsistent with the legislative intent and common sense. The first-instance judgment correctly found that Sun Lixing was injured within the workplace.

Regarding the issue of whether the appellee Sun Lixing fell "due to work-related reasons": The "due to work-related reasons" stipulated in Article 14 of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance means that there is a causal relationship between the employee's injury and the performance of his or her own work, i.e., the employee is injured because of engaging in his or her own work. Sun Lixing went down from the eighth-floor office of Zhongli Company in the Business Center to the first floor and fell at the steps of the first-floor entrance in order to complete the work task of driving to pick up someone. Sun Lixing fell while going downstairs, which was caused by completing the work task. The appellant Park Labor Bureau's argument that Sun Lixing was not injured while driving and therefore did not fall "due to work-related reasons" was untenable.

Regarding the issue of whether the appellee Sun Lixing's own negligence in walking affected the work-related injury determination: Article 16 of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance specifies three circumstances that do not constitute work-related injuries: injuries or deaths caused by crimes or violations of public security administration, injuries or deaths caused by intoxication, and self-inflicted injuries or suicide. Negligence in the course of work is not a statutory circumstance that precludes a work-related injury determination and does not affect the establishment of the causal relationship between the employee's injury and the performance of his or her own work. In work-related injury accidents, injured employees generally have some degree of negligence, such as carelessness or lack of concentration. If subjective negligence on the part of the employee were taken as an exclusionary condition for work-related injury determination, it would not only be inconsistent with the legislative intent of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance to protect the lawful rights and interests of workers, but also run counter to common life experience. Even if Sun Lixing was indeed careless in walking, it would not affect this work-related injury determination. The appellant Park Labor Bureau's assertion that the reason for Sun Lixing's fall was not slippery steps due to rain or snow but his own lack of concentration, and therefore Sun Lixing did not suffer injury "due to work-related reasons," was untenable.

Article 1 of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance stipulates: "This Regulation is formulated to ensure that employees who suffer accident injuries or occupational diseases due to work receive medical treatment and economic compensation, to promote the prevention of work-related injuries and occupational rehabilitation, and to disperse the risk of work-related injuries borne by employers." Article 1 of the Measures for Determining Work-Related Injuries also stipulates: "These Measures are formulated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance to standardize the procedures for determining work-related injuries, to carry out work-related injury determinations according to law, and to protect the lawful rights and interests of the parties concerned." This is the legislative purpose of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance and the Measures for Determining Work-Related Injuries. When applying the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance and the Measures for Determining Work-Related Injuries, labor and social security administrative organs should understand the specific provisions therein in light of the legislative purpose. In this case, the appellant Park Labor Bureau's understanding of the terms "workplace" and "due to work-related reasons" in Article 14(1) of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance did not conform to the legislative purpose of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance to protect the lawful rights and interests of employees. Article 1 of the Administrative Procedure Law stipulates: "This Law is formulated in accordance with the Constitution to ensure the correct and timely trial of administrative cases by the people's courts, to protect the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations, and to maintain and supervise the lawful exercise of administrative powers by administrative organs." This provision reflects the purpose of establishing the administrative litigation system in the state. When an administrative organ's understanding of the law deviates from the legislative intent, the people's court should, when trying the relevant administrative case, make a correct interpretation in accordance with the law, which is also a form of supervision over the exercise of administrative powers by administrative organs. The opinion of the original third party Zhongli Company that "in the absence of clear legal provisions, the understanding and application of the law should respect the understanding and determination of the appellant as an administrative organ" lacked legal basis and was therefore not adopted.

In summary, the first-instance judgment correctly found that the appellant Park Labor Bureau had applied the law incorrectly, and the judgment annulling the (2004) No. 0001 "Work-Related Injury Determination Decision" made by the Park Labor Bureau had clear factual findings, correct application of law, and lawful trial procedures, and should be upheld. Accordingly, the Tianjin High People's Court, in accordance with Article 61(1) of the Administrative Procedure Law, on July 11, 2005, rendered the following judgment:

Reject the appeal and affirm the original judgment.
